hook: Write a real formal e-mail, and have your own AI mark it line by line.
intro: Your first formal text in the course. You write the e-mail here, in the box, and the app builds a correction request that carries your own text. You paste that into your own AI, it corrects what you actually wrote, and you bring the score back. The up to four fixes it gives you are saved: your next speaking and writing exercises quietly bring one or two of them back, so the same slip does not survive for long. Aim for 400 to 900 characters, roughly the length of a real complaint e-mail. Much shorter and there is nothing to correct; much longer and you are writing an essay rather than an e-mail.
tips[0].title: The frame carries the register
tips[0].text: A formal e-mail is recognised by its frame before anyone reads the content. Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren when you do not know the name, Sehr geehrte Frau Weber when you do. Mit freundlichen Grüßen at the end, and no comma after it — the next line is your name. Sie, Ihnen and Ihr are capitalised all the way through.
tips[0].trap: After the greeting comes a comma and then a lower-case start: „Sehr geehrte Frau Weber,“ then „ich wende mich …“, not „Ich“.
tips[0].check.why: No comma follows the formal sign-off, and Liebe Grüße is for people you know.
tips[1].title: Ask, do not demand
tips[1].text: The request is where the register is won or lost. A bare imperative or a flat present tense reads as an order. Soften it with the Konjunktiv II: ich würde gern, ich hätte eine Frage, könnten Sie, wäre es möglich. The content stays exactly as firm; only the tone changes.
tips[1].trap: „Geben Sie mir mein Geld zurück“ is grammatical and will cost you the register marks. „Ich würde gern eine Rückerstattung beantragen“ asks for the same thing.
tips[1].check.why: Könnten with bitte is a request; the other two are orders.
tips[2].title: Five moves, in this order
tips[2].text: Greeting. Why you are writing. What happened, with the facts and the dates. What you want. A date for the answer, then the sign-off. An e-mail that follows those five moves is hard to mark down for structure, and the structure is what the correction looks at first.
tips[2].check.why: The greeting comes first, then one line saying why you are writing; the facts follow.
tips[2].visual.moves[0].label: Greeting
tips[2].visual.moves[1].label: Reason
tips[2].visual.moves[2].label: Details
tips[2].visual.moves[3].label: Request
tips[2].visual.moves[4].label: Close
remember[0]: Sehr geehrte … , then a lower-case start; Mit freundlichen Grüßen with no comma.
remember[1]: Soften every request: ich würde gern, könnten Sie, wäre es möglich.
remember[2]: Five moves: greeting, why, what happened, what you want, by when.
remember[3]: Sie, Ihnen and Ihr are always capitalised.
exam: A formal e-mail of this kind is the written task the B1 certificate sets, and the one letter everyone in Germany ends up writing sooner or later.
mistakes[0].why: No comma after the formal sign-off.
mistakes[1].why: After the greeting the sentence starts lower case.
mistakes[2].why: The same request, in the right register.
mistakes[3].why: The formal Sie is capitalised; sie would mean she or they.
tips[2].check.q: What belongs in the second move of a formal e-mail?
tips[2].check.options[2]: the date you want an answer by
